title: Georgia Smart Set, Bunk Johnson and White's own featured solos
summary: White recalls Bunk Johnson on the Georgia Smart Set and describes his own New Orleans-style features and triple-tongue solos.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: And? Tell us a little bit about the Georgia Smart Set, because this is a very close friend. I had Buck Johnson, who I remember.
Yeah, that's right. Thanks for them.
That's right. He never got to tell me anything about it. That's right.

So, you can tell me a little bit about it. Well, Buck, Buck served the season on the, on the Georgia Smart Set, uh, under Frank Moreland. Uh, and Buck was a featured man in the way he played. And Buck was a very fine jazz man. And he had a distinct way of, of playing the special numbers that Frank would allocate him to play at the Noonday concert was, was a, a send off to the band. The same as after, after I had spent a season in New Orleans down there, and I come to this later, because this is 1924 when I took a little squirt with the Alabama minstrels just for a few months. They featured me in the New Orleans style. And Eddie Howard. And I had to play a few numbers out there for Mr. Bowman, who was the manager of the show. He'd come out to hear these numbers, like the St. Louis Blues and the High Society. They liked to hear me play those numbers. And I was featured with them. But I also had to play an intricate solo at times too. I had also, I sometimes was called upon to play a decent solo, like a triple-tongue poker. And for those triple-tongue pokers, I played short and sweet, three-style poker, and, and my old Kentucky home. I played my old Kentucky home in my own variations, three variations. A six-eight movement, a two-four movement, and then the last movement, two-four, but the last eight or twelve or sixteen measures in triple-tongue. And then the last one, I was a kid. Now, I, uh, when I came out of the Army, well, I haven't told you about the Army in the first place. In Sedalia, Missouri, I'm with the Cole Brothers Circus, and the United States commissioners, investigators, came in the tent right after a horse had, I mean, the lions had almost ate of a horse in the surface. Well, Lizzie was on the surface then, and she had these beautiful pigeons on her shoulder that would light around as she paraded around in the pageant. Now, we have-
